title: Space Tech Briefing — July 31, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts! This is your daily dose of the cosmos, live from the Space Technology News Desk, and it is **July 31, 2026**. What an incredible week it's been, both for the future of space exploration and for the rising stars of the industry!

Let's dive right into some major recent developments that are still echoing across the space community.

First up, a look back at an event that's fueling the next generation of space pioneers! From July 11th to 18th, hundreds of young, aspiring engineers got a taste of the real space world at the **C'Space 2026** event. Held at the Ger military camp, this annual program saw participants launching their own rockets and miniature satellites. Imagine that! A whole week living and working like space engineers, getting hands-on experience that's absolutely critical. This initiative, backed by CNES, is doing an outstanding job of training the future architects of our space endeavors. It's truly inspiring to see so many bright minds already reaching for the stars!

And speaking of reaching for the stars, let's talk about a monumental step forward for heavy-lift rocketry! SpaceX has once again pushed boundaries with the **Starship Flight 13**. Launched on July 24th, UTC, this thirteenth test flight was a resounding success, hitting several crucial technical milestones. For the first time, Starship deployed its initial batch of **Starlink V3 satellites** – a significant upgrade for global internet connectivity. But that's not all! The mission also confirmed an in-flight engine relight and, in a truly impressive display of control, the upper stage executed a picture-perfect atmospheric re-entry, culminating in a soft splashdown right in the Indian Ocean. This flight officially validated the Raptor V3 engines in space, marking a colossal stride for the Starship program. The big question now, of course, is: will Flight 14 be the one to attempt that elusive first orbital mission? We are all on the edge of our seats!

What a week for space! From fostering young talent to achieving new heights in rocket technology, the pace of innovation is simply breathtaking.

That's all for your morning space briefing today, July 31, 2026. Stay curious, keep looking up, and we'll catch you tomorrow with more incredible stories from beyond our world. Have a fantastic day!
